learn.b: Say Hola for hello. Use Buenos días in the morning, Buenas tardes in the afternoon and Buenas noches at night. To say goodbye, use Adiós or Hasta luego (see you later).
To say your name, use Me llamo and then your name. Me llamo Ana means My name is Ana. To ask someone, say ¿Cómo te llamas?
Ask ¿Cómo estás? to say How are you? You can answer Bien, gracias (Fine, thanks). Say por favor for please, gracias for thank you and de nada for you're welcome.

qs.q: How do you say 'good morning' in Spanish?
qs.why: Buenos días is used to greet people in the morning.

qs.q: What does 'Me llamo Ana' mean?
qs.why: Me llamo means 'my name is'.

qs.q: Which word means 'thank you'?
qs.why: Gracias is the Spanish word for thank you.

qs.q: How can you answer '¿Cómo estás?' if you feel fine?
qs.why: Bien, gracias means 'Fine, thanks'.

qs.q: 'Adiós' means 'goodbye'.
qs.why: Adiós is a common way to say goodbye.

qs.q: Match each Spanish word to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'Hello, my name is Luis'

lab.q: Challenge: type 'thank you' in Spanish.
lab.hint: One word, it starts with g.

lab.q: Challenge: how do you say 'My name is Marta'?
Challenge: translate 'Buenas noches' into English.
lab.why: Buenas noches is used in the evening and at night.

learn.b: Count like this: uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez. Use them for ages, prices and addresses.
Rojo is red, azul is blue, verde is green and amarillo is yellow. Colors usually come after the noun, like la manzana roja (the red apple).
Learn el pan (bread), el agua (water), la manzana (apple) and la leche (milk). To ask for something, say Quiero and then the thing. Quiero agua means I want water.

qs.q: What is 'cinco' in English?
qs.why: Cinco is the number five.

qs.q: Which word means 'blue'?
qs.why: Azul means blue; rojo is red and verde is green.

qs.q: What does 'la manzana' mean?
qs.why: La manzana is the apple.

qs.q: How do you say 'I want water'?
qs.why: Quiero means 'I want', so Quiero agua is 'I want water'.

qs.q: 'Siete' means seven.
qs.why: Siete is the number seven.

qs.q: Match each number to its meaning
Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest

lab.q: Challenge: type the Spanish word for the number 7.
Challenge: type the Spanish word for the color red.
Challenge: translate 'I want water' into Spanish.
lab.why: Quiero agua means I want water.

learn.b: Learn la madre (mother), el padre (father), el hermano (brother) and la hermana (sister). Words with el are masculine and words with la are feminine.
Ser has the forms soy (I am), eres (you are) and es (he or she is). Yo soy estudiante means I am a student.
Tener has the forms tengo (I have), tienes (you have) and tiene (he or she has). Tengo un hermano means I have a brother.

qs.q: What does 'la hermana' mean?
qs.why: La hermana means the sister.

qs.q: Complete: Yo ___ estudiante. (I am a student)
qs.why: Soy is the 'I' form of ser (to be).

qs.q: How do you say 'I have a brother'?
qs.why: Tengo is the 'I' form of tener (to have).

qs.q: Complete: Ella ___ dos gatos. (She has two cats)
qs.why: Tiene is the 'he or she' form of tener.

qs.q: 'El padre' means 'the father'.
qs.why: El padre is the father.

qs.q: Match each family word to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'I have two sisters'

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'the sister' into Spanish.
Challenge: complete with ser: Ella ___ mi madre.
lab.hint: Use the he/she form of ser.
lab.why: Ella es mi madre: she is my mother.

lab.q: Challenge: complete with tener: Yo ___ dos gatos.
lab.hint: Use the yo form of tener.

learn.b: Use el or la for 'the' with one thing and los or las for many. Un and una mean 'a'. To make most plurals, add -s: libro becomes libros.
The days are lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado and domingo. They are not written with a capital letter in Spanish.
Use ¿Dónde está...? to ask where something is. ¿Dónde está la escuela? means Where is the school? Remember la casa (house) and la escuela (school) use la.

qs.q: Which article goes with 'casa' (house)?
qs.why: Casa is feminine, so it uses la.

qs.q: What is the plural of 'libro'?
qs.why: Add -s to most words that end in a vowel: libros.

qs.q: What does 'miércoles' mean?
qs.why: Miércoles is Wednesday.

qs.q: What does '¿Dónde está la escuela?' ask?
qs.why: Dónde means 'where'.

qs.q: 'Sábado' means Sunday.
qs.why: Sábado is Saturday; Sunday is domingo.

qs.q: Match each day to its meaning
Put these days in order, starting from Monday

lab.q: Challenge: type 'Monday' in Spanish.
lab.hint: It starts with l and ends in -s.

lab.q: Challenge: type the plural article: ___ libros (the books).
lab.why: Libro is masculine, so los libros.

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'Where is the school?' into Spanish.
lab.why: ¿Dónde está la escuela? asks where the school is.

learn.b: In Spanish, an adjective matches its noun. Many end in -o for masculine and -a for feminine. Add -s for plural: el gato negro, la casa blanca, los gatos negros.
Adjectives usually come after the noun: un coche rojo (a red car), una chica simpática (a nice girl). Learn alto (tall), bajo (short), nuevo (new), viejo (old) and simpático (nice).
Adjectives ending in -e or a consonant stay the same for masculine and feminine: un perro grande, una casa grande. Add -s for plural: grandes. Add -es after a consonant: fácil becomes fáciles.

qs.q: Which phrase means 'the white house'?
qs.why: Casa is feminine, so the adjective ends in -a.

qs.q: Choose the correct form: los gatos ___ (black).
qs.why: Gatos is masculine plural, so use negros.

qs.q: What does 'alto' mean?
qs.why: Alto means tall.

qs.q: Which adjective has the same form for masculine and feminine?
qs.why: Adjectives ending in -e do not change for gender.

qs.q: In Spanish, adjectives usually come before the noun.
qs.why: They usually come after the noun: un coche rojo.

qs.q: Match each adjective to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'I have a red car'

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'a big house' into Spanish.
lab.hint: Casa is feminine; grande does not change.
lab.why: Una casa grande: the adjective follows the noun.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Las chicas son ___ (tall).
lab.why: Chicas is feminine plural, so altas.

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'the new books' into Spanish.
lab.hint: Libro is masculine; nuevo goes after.

learn.b: To use a regular -ar verb, drop -ar and add endings: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan. Hablo español means I speak Spanish.
For -er verbs, use -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en: como, comes, come. For -ir verbs, use -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en: vivo, vives, vive.
The pronouns are yo, tú, él/ella, nosotros, vosotros and ellos/ellas. Spanish often drops them because the ending shows who does the action: Trabajamos hoy means We work today.

qs.q: Which sentence means 'I speak Spanish'?
qs.why: Hablo is the yo form of hablar.

qs.q: Complete: Ella ___ pan. (comer)
qs.why: Ella uses the él/ella form: come.

qs.q: Complete: Nosotros ___ en Madrid. (vivir)
qs.why: Nosotros takes -imos for -ir verbs.

qs.q: What does 'bebes' mean?
qs.why: -es is the tú ending, so bebes means you drink.

qs.q: 'Trabajan' means 'they work'.
qs.why: -an is the ellos ending of -ar verbs.

qs.q: Match each verb form to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'Ana lives in Madrid'

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Yo ___ (trabajar) en una tienda.
lab.hint: Yo form of an -ar verb ends in -o.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Tú ___ (beber) agua.
lab.hint: Tú form of an -er verb ends in -es.

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'They live in Italy' into Spanish.
lab.hint: Use the ellos form of vivir.

learn.b: Use ser for identity, origin, jobs and descriptions: Soy Ana. Soy de Italia. Es alto. The forms are soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son.
Use estar for place and feelings or states: Estoy en casa. Estoy cansado (I am tired). The forms are estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están.
¿De dónde eres? Soy de Italia uses ser for origin. ¿Cómo estás? Estoy bien uses estar for feelings. Hoy es lunes uses ser for the day. Madrid está en España uses estar for place.

qs.q: Complete: ___ de Italia. (I am from Italy)
qs.why: Origin uses ser: soy de.

qs.q: Complete: Madrid ___ en España.
qs.why: Location uses estar.

qs.q: Which sentence says 'I am tired'?
qs.why: Feelings and states use estar.

qs.q: Complete: Nosotros ___ estudiantes.
qs.why: Identity uses ser: nosotros somos.

qs.q: Spanish uses estar to say where something is.
qs.why: Place uses estar: El libro está en la mesa.

qs.q: Match each form to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'She is from Mexico'

lab.q: Challenge: complete with ser: Yo ___ de Italia.
Challenge: complete with estar: El libro ___ en la mesa.
lab.why: El libro está en la mesa.

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'We are happy' into Spanish.

learn.b: Ask ¿Qué hora es? For one o'clock say Es la una. For other hours say Son las dos, Son las tres. Add y media (half past), y cuarto (quarter past) or menos cuarto (quarter to).
The months are enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre and diciembre. They are not written with a capital letter.
The seasons are la primavera (spring), el verano (summer), el otoño (autumn) and el invierno (winter). For dates, say Es el cinco de mayo (It is the fifth of May).

qs.q: How do you say 'It is three o'clock'?
qs.why: Use son las for all hours except one.

qs.q: What does 'y media' add to the time?
qs.why: Y media means and a half.

qs.q: Which month is 'junio'?
qs.why: Junio is June.

qs.q: Which season is 'invierno'?
qs.why: Invierno means winter.

qs.q: 'Es la una' means 'It is one o'clock'.
qs.why: Es la una is the only hour that uses es and la.

qs.q: Match each season to its meaning
Put the months in order

lab.q: Challenge: type 'July' in Spanish.
lab.hint: It looks like the English word.

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'It is two thirty' into Spanish.
lab.hint: Use Son las + hour + y media.

lab.q: Challenge: type 'summer' in Spanish.

learn.b: Learn la ciudad (city), la calle (street), el banco (bank), el parque (park), la tienda (shop), el mercado (market), la biblioteca (library) and el supermercado (supermarket).
Use qué (what), quién (who), dónde (where), cuándo (when), por qué (why), cómo (how) and cuánto (how much). Questions have ¿ at the start and ? at the end.
Ir means to go: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. Say ir a + place: Voy a la tienda. A + el becomes al: Voy al parque.

qs.q: How do you say 'Where do you live?'
qs.why: Dónde asks where.

qs.q: Complete: Nosotros ___ al parque. (ir)
qs.why: Nosotros goes with vamos.

qs.q: Complete: Voy ___ parque.
qs.why: A + el always becomes al.

qs.q: What does '¿Por qué?' mean?
qs.why: Por qué means why.

qs.q: '¿Cuándo?' asks about a place.
qs.why: Cuándo asks about time. Dónde asks about place.

qs.q: Match each question word to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'Ana goes to the bank'

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'the library' into Spanish.
Challenge: type the Spanish words for 'why' (two words).
lab.hint: It has two words in a question.

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Yo ___ al mercado. (ir)

learn.b: Learn la casa (house), la cocina (kitchen), el dormitorio (bedroom), el baño (bathroom), la sala (living room) and el jardín (garden). Use en to say where: Estoy en la cocina.
Learn la camisa (shirt), los pantalones (trousers), el vestido (dress), los zapatos (shoes) and la chaqueta (jacket). Use llevar for to wear: Llevo una camisa azul.
Ask ¿Qué tiempo hace? Say Hace sol (sunny), Hace frío (cold) or Hace calor (hot). For rain and snow use verbs: Llueve (it rains), Nieva (it snows).

qs.q: How do you say 'It is cold'?
qs.why: Frío means cold.

qs.q: What are 'los zapatos'?
qs.why: Zapatos means shoes.

qs.q: What is 'la cocina'?
qs.why: Cocina means kitchen.

qs.q: In which room do you usually sleep?
qs.why: Dormitorio means bedroom.

qs.q: 'Llueve' means 'It is snowing'.
qs.why: Llueve means it rains. Nieva means it snows.

qs.q: Match each clothing word to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'Today it is very hot'

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'It is sunny' into Spanish.
Challenge: type 'kitchen' in Spanish.
Challenge: translate 'the dress' into Spanish.

learn.b: For -ar verbs, use -é, -aste, -ó: hablé (I spoke), hablaste (you spoke), habló (he or she spoke). For -er and -ir verbs, use -í, -iste, -ió: comí (I ate).

learn.h: Ir and ser in the past
learn.b: Ir (to go) and ser (to be) share the same past forms: fui, fuiste, fue. Context tells you which one is meant. Fui al cine means I went to the cinema.
Use ayer (yesterday), anoche (last night), la semana pasada (last week) and el año pasado (last year). They show that the action is finished.

qs.q: Complete: Ayer yo ___ pizza. (I ate)
qs.why: Comí is the past 'I' form of comer.

qs.q: What does 'hablaste' mean?
qs.why: The ending -aste is the past 'you' form.

qs.q: What does 'Fui al cine anoche' mean?
o: I went to the movies last night
I go to the movies every night
I will go to the movies tonight
I was at the movies last week
qs.why: Fui is 'I went' and anoche is 'last night'.

qs.q: Which word means 'yesterday'?
qs.why: Ayer means yesterday; anoche means last night.

qs.q: 'Ella comió' means 'She ate'.
qs.why: Comió is the past 'he or she' form of comer.

qs.q: Match each time word to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'Yesterday I ate pizza'

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Ayer yo ___ (hablar) con Ana.
lab.hint: Preterite yo form of -ar verbs ends in -é.

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'I ate pizza' into Spanish.
Challenge: complete: Ayer nosotros ___ (ir) al cine.
lab.hint: Ir uses the same past forms as ser.

learn.b: Use a la derecha (to the right), a la izquierda (to the left) and todo recto (straight ahead). La esquina is the corner.
Cerca de means near and lejos de means far from. To ask the way, say ¿Cómo llego a la estación? (How do I get to the station?).
Learn el aeropuerto (airport), el billete (ticket), la estación (station) and la habitación (room). Use reservar to say to book.

qs.q: What does 'a la izquierda' mean?
qs.why: Izquierda means left.

qs.q: What does 'todo recto' mean?
qs.why: Todo recto means straight ahead.

qs.q: How do you ask 'How do I get to the station?'
qs.why: ¿Cómo llego a...? is the usual way to ask for directions.

qs.q: What is 'la habitación' at a hotel?
qs.why: La habitación means the room.

qs.q: 'Lejos de' means 'far from'.
qs.why: Lejos means far; cerca means near.

qs.q: Match each word to its meaning
Put these travel steps in a logical order

lab.q: Challenge: type 'to the left' in Spanish.
Challenge: type 'straight ahead' in Spanish.
Challenge: translate 'The airport is far' into Spanish.

learn.b: Use me gusta with one thing and me gustan with many things. Me gusta el cine means I like cinema. Me gustan los libros means I like books. Say no me gusta for I don't like.
Say creo que or pienso que to mean I think that. Say estoy de acuerdo for I agree and no estoy de acuerdo for I disagree.
Prefiero means I prefer. Porque means because, and más que means more than. Prefiero el té al café means I prefer tea to coffee.

qs.q: Which sentence means 'I like the books'?
qs.why: Books are plural, so use me gustan.

qs.q: What does 'Estoy de acuerdo' mean?
qs.why: Estoy de acuerdo means I agree.

qs.q: How do you say 'I think that it is good'?
qs.why: Creo que + a sentence means 'I think that...'.

qs.q: What does 'Prefiero el té al café' express?
o: A preference for tea over coffee
qs.why: Prefiero means 'I prefer'.

qs.q: 'Porque' means 'because'.
qs.why: Porque (one word) introduces a reason.

qs.q: Match each phrase to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'I think that cinema is fun'

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Me ___ los libros. (gustar)
Challenge: translate 'I think that it is good' into Spanish.
Challenge: translate 'I prefer tea' into Spanish.

learn.b: Use ir a + a verb to talk about plans: voy a viajar means I am going to travel. Add words like mañana (tomorrow) or el próximo año (next year).
Reflexive verbs use me: me levanto (I get up), me ducho (I shower) and me acuesto (I go to bed). Add the time with a la una or a las siete.
The imperfect tense talks about habits in the past. Jugaba means I used to play. Use words like siempre (always) and de niño (as a child).

qs.q: Complete: Mañana ___ a viajar. (I'm going to travel)
qs.why: Voy a + verb expresses a plan for the future.

qs.q: What does 'Me levanto a las siete' mean?
o: I go to bed at seven
qs.why: Me levanto means 'I get up'.

qs.q: Which form means 'I used to play'?
qs.why: Jugaba is the imperfect form for past habits.

qs.q: What does 'el próximo año' mean?
qs.why: Próximo means next.

qs.q: 'Me acuesto' means 'I wake up'.
qs.why: Me acuesto means I go to bed.

qs.q: Match each phrase to its meaning
Put this morning routine in a logical order

lab.q: Challenge: translate 'I am going to travel' into Spanish.
Challenge: complete: Nosotros ___ a comer. (ir)
Challenge: complete: Yo ___ a las siete. (levantarse)

learn.b: The imperfect has easy endings. For -ar verbs: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban (jugaba). For -er and -ir verbs: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían (comía, vivía).
Only three verbs are irregular. Ser: era, eras, era, éramos, eran. Ir: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban. Ver: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veían.
Use the imperfect for habits, descriptions and background in the past: Cuando era niño, jugaba cada día. Use the preterite for a single finished event: Ayer jugué al fútbol.

qs.q: Complete: Cuando era niña, yo ___ en el parque. (jugar)
qs.why: A repeated past habit uses the imperfect.

qs.q: Which is the imperfect of 'comer' for ellos?
qs.why: -ían is the ellos ending for -er verbs.

qs.q: What is the imperfect of 'ir' for yo?
qs.why: Ir has the imperfect iba.

qs.q: Which sentence describes a habit in the past?
o: Todos los veranos íbamos a la playa
qs.why: Todos los veranos shows a repeated habit.

qs.q: The imperfect is used for a single finished action.
qs.why: A single finished action uses the preterite.

qs.q: Match each form to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'When I was little I used to play'

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Yo ___ (vivir) en Roma de niño.
lab.hint: Yo form of -ir verbs ends in -ía.

lab.q: Challenge: complete with ser: Nosotros ___ amigos.
Challenge: translate 'She used to read every night' into Spanish.

learn.b: Some verbs change stem in the preterite: tener becomes tuve, hacer becomes hice, decir becomes dije, venir becomes vine, poder becomes pude. The endings are -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron, with no accents.
Hacer has hizo for él or ella. Verbs with j in the stem, like decir and traer, use -eron: dijeron, trajeron. Estar becomes estuve and poner becomes puse.
Use he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + a past participle: he comido (I have eaten). Participles end in -ado or -ido. Some are irregular: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, puesto, abierto.

qs.q: What is the preterite of 'tener' for yo?
qs.why: Tener becomes tuve in the preterite.

qs.q: Complete: Ayer ella ___ la tarea. (hacer)
qs.why: Hacer has hizo for ella in the preterite.

qs.q: Complete: Yo ___ comido paella.
qs.why: Yo goes with he + participle.

qs.q: What is the past participle of 'escribir'?
qs.why: Escribir has the irregular participle escrito.

qs.q: The past participle of 'ver' is 'visto'.
qs.why: Visto is irregular.

qs.q: Match each form to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'I have already eaten'

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Ayer yo no ___ (poder) venir.
Challenge: type the past participle of 'hacer'.
Challenge: translate 'I have seen the film' into Spanish.

learn.b: To compare, use más + adjective + que (more than), menos + adjective + que (less than) and tan + adjective + como (as ... as). Ana es más alta que Luis. Luis es tan simpático como Ana.
Four adjectives are irregular: bueno becomes mejor (better), malo becomes peor (worse), grande can become mayor (older) and pequeño can become menor (younger). Do not say más mejor.
For the most or the least, use el/la/los/las más + adjective: la más alta de la clase. Use el mejor for the best. Use tanto/tanta/tantos/tantas ... como for amounts: Tengo tantos libros como tú.

qs.q: Which sentence means 'Ana is taller than Luis'?
o: Ana es más alta como Luis
Ana es tan alta que Luis
Ana es más alta que Luis
Ana es alta más que Luis
qs.why: Use más + adjective + que.

qs.q: What does 'mejor' mean?
qs.why: Mejor is the comparative of bueno.

qs.q: How do you say 'as tall as'?
qs.why: Equal comparisons use tan ... como.

qs.q: Which sentence means 'He is the best student in the class'?
o: Es el más mejor estudiante de la clase
Es el mejor estudiante de la clase
Es el tan bueno estudiante de la clase
Es el muy bueno estudiante de la clase
qs.why: Use el mejor, never más mejor.

qs.q: 'Menor' can mean 'younger'.
qs.why: Menor is used for younger, and mayor for older.

qs.q: Match each word to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'My house is bigger than yours'

lab.q: Challenge: type 'worse' in Spanish.
Challenge: complete: Mi hermano es ___ alto que yo. (taller)
Challenge: translate 'She is as intelligent as him' into Spanish.
a: ella es tan inteligente como él
ella es tan inteligente como el

learn.b: These replace the thing or person: me, te, lo, la, nos, os, los, las. Yo leo el libro becomes Yo lo leo. Compro las manzanas becomes Las compro. They go before the verb.
With an infinitive, put the pronoun before the first verb or attach it to the infinitive: Lo quiero ver or Quiero verlo (I want to see it).
Indirect pronouns say to or for whom: me, te, le, nos, os, les. Le doy un regalo means I give her a gift. With lo or la after le or les, use se: Se lo doy (I give it to him).

qs.q: Replace 'el libro': Yo leo el libro. Yo ___ leo.
qs.why: El libro is masculine singular, so lo.

qs.q: Replace 'las manzanas': Compro las manzanas.
qs.why: Las manzanas is feminine plural, so las.

qs.q: Complete: ___ doy un regalo a Ana. (I give Ana a gift)
qs.why: Le is the indirect pronoun for one person.

qs.q: Which sentence means 'I want to see it' (el museo)?
qs.why: Attach lo to the infinitive.

qs.q: 'Se lo doy' replaces 'Le lo doy'.
qs.why: Le or les becomes se before lo, la, los or las.

qs.q: Match each pronoun to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'I give it to you'

lab.q: Challenge: replace the noun: Compro la camisa. ___ compro.
Challenge: translate 'I see you' (informal) into Spanish.
Challenge: replace both nouns: Doy el libro a Ana. ___ ___ doy.

learn.b: Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án to the whole infinitive: hablaré, comerás, viviremos. Mañana viajaré a Roma means Tomorrow I will travel to Rome.
Some verbs change the stem but keep the same endings: tener becomes tendr-, hacer har-, decir dir-, poder podr-, venir vendr-, salir saldr-, querer querr-, saber sabr-. Tendré means I will have.
For would, add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the same stem: hablaría, comería, tendría. Use it for polite requests and imagined situations: Me gustaría un café. Yo viajaría por el mundo.

qs.q: What is the future of 'hablar' for yo?
qs.why: Future: infinitive + é.

qs.q: Complete: El próximo año ellos ___ en Madrid. (vivir)
qs.why: Future ellos: infinitive + án.

qs.q: What is the future of 'tener' for él?
qs.why: Tener has the stem tendr-.

qs.q: How do you politely say 'I would like a coffee'?
qs.why: Gustaría is the conditional.

qs.q: The future tense of 'hacer' is 'haré'.
qs.why: Hacer uses the stem har-.

qs.q: Match each form to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'Tomorrow I will travel to Rome'

lab.q: Challenge: complete: Yo ___ (comer) pasta mañana.

learn.b: For a positive tú command, use the él form: habla (speak), come (eat), escribe (write). Eight verbs are irregular: ven, di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten. Ven aquí means Come here.
For a negative tú command, use no + the subjunctive form: no hables, no comas, no vengas. No comas tan rápido means Don't eat so fast.

Take the yo form, drop -o and add the opposite vowel: -ar verbs use -e, -es, -e, -emos, -en; -er and -ir verbs use -a, -as, -a, -amos, -an. Use it after quiero que, espero que and es importante que: Quiero que hables.

learn.b: Say Bonjour for hello or good day, and Salut for a casual hi. Use Bonsoir in the evening and Bonne nuit before bed. To say goodbye, use Au revoir.
Say Je m'appelle and your name: Je m'appelle Léa means My name is Léa. Ask Comment ça va ? to say How are you? and answer Ça va bien.
Merci means thank you and De rien means you're welcome. S'il vous plaît means please. It is the polite form you use with adults or strangers.

qs.q: How do you say 'good evening' in French?
qs.why: Bonsoir is used to greet people in the evening.

qs.q: What does 'Je m'appelle Léa' mean?
qs.why: Je m'appelle means 'my name is'.

qs.q: Which phrase means 'please' (polite)?
qs.why: S'il vous plaît is the polite way to say please.

qs.q: What does 'Comment ça va ?' ask?
qs.why: Comment ça va ? means 'How are you?'.

qs.q: 'Au revoir' means 'hello'.
qs.why: Au revoir means goodbye.

learn.b: Count like this: un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix. Use them for ages, prices and phone numbers.
Rouge is red, bleu is blue, vert is green and jaune is yellow. Colors usually come after the noun: la pomme rouge means the red apple.
Learn le pain (bread), l'eau (water), la pomme (apple) and le lait (milk). To ask politely, say Je voudrais. Je voudrais de l'eau means I would like some water.

learn.b: Learn la mère (mother), le père (father), le frère (brother) and la sœur (sister). Le goes with masculine words and la with feminine words.
Être has the forms je suis (I am), tu es (you are) and il est (he is). Je suis étudiant means I am a student.
Avoir has the forms j'ai (I have), tu as (you have) and il a (he has). J'ai un frère means I have a brother.

qs.q: What does 'la sœur' mean?
qs.why: La sœur means the sister.

qs.q: Complete: Je ___ étudiant. (I am a student)
qs.why: Suis is the 'I' form of être (to be).

qs.q: How do you say 'I have a brother'?
qs.why: J'ai is the 'I' form of avoir (to have).

qs.q: Complete: Elle ___ deux chats. (She has two cats)

qs.q: 'Le père' means 'the father'.

learn.b: Use le or la for 'the' with one thing and les for many. Un and une mean 'a'. Most plurals add -s, which you do not pronounce: livre becomes livres.
The days are lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi and dimanche. In French they are written with a small first letter.
Use Où est...? to ask where something is. Où est l'école ? means Where is the school? La maison (house) and l'école (school) are both feminine.

qs.q: Which article goes with 'maison' (house)?

qs.q: What is the plural of 'livre'?
qs.why: Most plurals add -s: livres.

qs.q: What does 'mercredi' mean?
qs.why: Mercredi is Wednesday.

qs.q: What does 'Où est l'école ?' ask?
qs.why: Où means 'where'.

qs.q: 'Samedi' means Sunday.
qs.why: Samedi is Saturday; Sunday is dimanche.

learn.b: In French, adjectives change with the noun. For feminine, add -e: petit becomes petite. For plural, add -s: petits, petites. Un garçon grand, une fille grande, des filles grandes.
Most adjectives come after the noun: une voiture rouge (a red car). A few short common ones come before: petit, grand, bon, beau, jeune, vieux, nouveau, joli. Say un petit chat, une grande maison.
Some adjectives change more: beau becomes belle, nouveau becomes nouvelle, blanc becomes blanche, heureux becomes heureuse. Adjectives ending in -e, like rouge, stay the same.

qs.q: Which phrase means 'a small cat'?
qs.why: Petit comes before the noun.

qs.q: What is the feminine singular of 'grand'?
qs.why: Add -e for feminine.

qs.why: Blanc becomes blanche for feminine singular.

qs.why: Colors come after the noun.

learn.b: Drop -er and add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. Parler gives je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. Before a vowel, je becomes j': j'aime, j'habite.
Regular -ir verbs like finir use -is, -is, -it, -issons, -issez, -issent: je finis, nous finissons. Regular -re verbs like vendre use -s, -s, nothing, -ons, -ez, -ent: je vends, il vend.
Learn aimer (to like), habiter (to live), travailler (to work), manger (to eat), choisir (to choose) and attendre (to wait). For manger, nous writes mangeons, with an e.

qs.q: Complete: Nous ___ français. (parler)

qs.q: Complete: Tu ___ tôt ? (finir)

learn.b: Put ne ... pas around the verb: Je ne parle pas anglais. Before a vowel, ne becomes n': Je n'aime pas le poisson. After a negative, un, une and des become de: Je n'ai pas de frère.
There are three ways. Raise your voice: Tu parles français ? Add est-ce que: Est-ce que tu parles français ? Or flip the verb and pronoun: Parles-tu français ? The second one is the easiest.
Learn où (where), quand (when), pourquoi (why), comment (how), qui (who), combien (how much) and qu'est-ce que (what). Où habites-tu ? means Where do you live?

qs.q: How do you say 'I don't speak English'?

learn.b: Aller means to go: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont. Say aller à + place: Je vais à l'école. Remember à + le = au and à + les = aux: Je vais au parc.
Faire means to do or to make: je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font. Use it for activities: faire du sport, faire la cuisine, faire des courses (to go shopping).

Learn la banque (bank), le marché (market), la gare (station), la bibliothèque (library), le parc (park) and la ville (city). Use à for cities (à Paris), en for feminine countries (en France) and au for masculine ones (au Canada).

qs.why: Vous goes with faites.

learn.b: Ask Quelle heure est-il ? Say Il est une heure for one o'clock and Il est trois heures for three o'clock. Add et quart (quarter past), et demie (half past) or moins le quart (quarter to). Midi is noon and minuit is midnight.
The months are janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre and décembre. They are not written with a capital letter.
The seasons are le printemps, l'été, l'automne and l'hiver. Say au printemps, en été, en automne, en hiver. For dates, say C'est le cinq mai. For the first day, say le premier mai.

learn.b: Learn la maison (house), la cuisine (kitchen), la chambre (bedroom), la salle de bains (bathroom), le salon (living room) and le jardin (garden). Use dans for in: Je suis dans la cuisine.
Learn la chemise (shirt), le pantalon (trousers), la robe (dress), les chaussures (shoes) and la veste (jacket). Use porter for to wear: Je porte une chemise bleue.
Ask Quel temps fait-il ? Say Il fait beau (nice), Il fait chaud (hot) or Il fait froid (cold). For rain and snow use these verbs: Il pleut (it rains), Il neige (it snows).

learn.b: Most verbs use avoir plus a past participle. J'ai mangé means I ate. Nous avons parlé means we spoke. For -er verbs, the participle ends in -é.
Some verbs of movement, like aller (to go) and arriver (to arrive), use être. Je suis allé au cinéma means I went to the cinema. A girl writes allée.
Use hier (yesterday), ce matin (this morning), la semaine dernière (last week) and l'année dernière (last year). They show the action is finished.

qs.q: Complete: Hier, j'___ une pizza. (I ate)
qs.why: J'ai mangé is the passé composé of manger.

qs.why: Nous avons parlé is the past tense: we spoke.

qs.q: 'Je suis allé au cinéma' means 'I went to the cinema'.

learn.b: Use à gauche (to the left), à droite (to the right) and tout droit (straight ahead). Au coin means at the corner.
Près de means near and loin de means far from. To ask the way, say Comment aller à la gare ? (How do I get to the station?).
Learn la gare (train station), l'aéroport (airport), le billet (ticket) and la chambre (room). Use réserver for to book.

qs.q: What is 'la chambre' in a hotel?

qs.q: 'Près de' means 'far from'.

learn.b: Use j'aime (I like), j'adore (I love) and je déteste (I hate). J'aime le cinéma means I like cinema. Add ne...pas for the negative: je n'aime pas.
Say je pense que or à mon avis to mean I think that or in my opinion. Say je suis d'accord for I agree and je ne suis pas d'accord for I disagree.
Je préfère means I prefer. Parce que means because, and plus...que means more than. Le film est plus long que le livre means the film is longer than the book.

qs.q: What does 'Je suis d'accord' mean?
qs.why: Je suis d'accord means I agree.

qs.why: Parce que introduces a reason.

qs.q: What does 'à mon avis' mean?

qs.q: 'Je déteste' means 'I love'.
qs.why: Je déteste means I hate.

learn.b: Use aller + a verb to talk about plans: je vais voyager means I am going to travel. Add words like demain (tomorrow) or l'année prochaine (next year).
Reflexive verbs use me: je me lève (I get up), je me douche (I shower) and je me couche (I go to bed). Add the time with à sept heures.
The imparfait talks about habits in the past. Je jouais means I used to play. Use words like toujours (always) and quand j'étais petit (when I was little).

learn.b: Take the nous form of the present, drop -ons, and add -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. Parlons gives je parlais, nous parlions, ils parlaient.
Only être has a special stem: j'étais, tu étais, il était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils étaient. Avoir and faire are regular: j'avais, je faisais.
Use the imparfait for habits, descriptions and background: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais au foot. Use the passé composé for a finished event: Hier, j'ai joué au foot.

qs.q: Complete: Quand j'étais petit, je ___ au foot. (jouer)
qs.why: A past habit uses the imparfait.

qs.q: What is the imparfait of 'avoir' for nous?

qs.q: What is the imparfait of 'être' for ils?

Demain, nous irons à la mer
Nous allons à la mer maintenant
Chaque été, nous allions à la mer
qs.why: Chaque été shows a repeated habit.

qs.q: The imparfait is used for a single finished event.
qs.why: A single finished event uses the passé composé.

learn.b: Many common verbs have irregular participles: avoir becomes eu, être becomes été, faire becomes fait, prendre becomes pris, voir becomes vu, boire becomes bu, dire becomes dit, écrire becomes écrit, mettre becomes mis, lire becomes lu.
In the passé composé, ne ... pas goes around the helper verb: Je n'ai pas mangé. Use déjà (already) and jamais (never): Tu as déjà visité Paris ? Je n'ai jamais pris le train.
Use the imparfait for the background and the passé composé for events. Il pleuvait quand je suis sorti means It was raining when I went out.

qs.why: Faire has the irregular participle fait.

qs.q: What is the past participle of 'prendre'?
qs.why: Prendre has the irregular participle pris.

Je ne vu pas le film
Je pas ai vu le film
Je n'ai pas vu le film
qs.why: Ne ... pas goes around ai.

learn.b: Use plus + adjective + que (more than), moins + adjective + que (less than) and aussi + adjective + que (as ... as). Elle est plus grande que lui. Il est aussi sympa qu'elle.
Bon becomes meilleur (better) as an adjective: ce gâteau est meilleur. Bien becomes mieux (better) as an adverb: elle chante mieux. Mauvais can become pire (worse).
For the most or the least, add le, la or les: le plus grand, la plus grande, le moins cher, le meilleur. For amounts use plus de, moins de, autant de: J'ai plus de livres que toi.

qs.q: Complete: Ana est ___ grande que Luc. (taller)

qs.q: How do you say 'as tall as'?
qs.why: Equal comparisons use aussi ... que.

qs.q: How do you say 'the biggest' (masculine)?
qs.why: Le agrees with a masculine noun.

qs.q: 'Mieux' is the comparative of 'bien'.
qs.why: Bien becomes mieux.

learn.b: These replace the thing or person: me, te, le, la, l', nous, vous, les. Je lis le livre becomes Je le lis. They go before the verb: Je les vois. With an infinitive, they go before the infinitive: Je veux le voir.
Use me, te, lui, nous, vous, leur for to someone: Je parle à Marie becomes Je lui parle. Je parle à mes amis becomes Je leur parle. Lui means to him or to her.
Y replaces à + a place or thing: Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'y vais. En replaces de + noun or an amount: Tu veux du pain ? Oui, j'en veux. They also go before the verb.

qs.q: Replace 'le livre': Je lis le livre. Je ___ lis.

qs.q: Replace 'à Marie': Je parle à Marie. Je ___ parle.
qs.why: Lui means to her or to him.

qs.why: Leur is the indirect pronoun for they.

learn.b: Add -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont to the whole infinitive: je parlerai, tu finiras, nous vendrons (drop the final e). Demain, j'irai à Paris means Tomorrow I will go to Paris.
Some verbs have a special stem but the same endings: être ser-, avoir aur-, aller ir-, faire fer-, voir verr-, venir viendr-, pouvoir pourr-, vouloir voudr-. Je serai, il aura, nous ferons.

For would, use the same stem plus -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: je parlerais, j'irais, je voudrais. Use it for politeness: Je voudrais un café. For imagined situations use si + imparfait: Si j'avais de l'argent, je voyagerais.

qs.q: What is the futur of 'parler' for je?
qs.why: Futur: infinitive + ai.

qs.q: What is the futur of 'aller' for nous?
qs.why: Aller has the stem ir-.

qs.q: Complete: Si j'avais un million, je ___ le monde. (voyager)
qs.why: Si + imparfait leads to the conditional.

qs.q: How do you politely say 'I would like a coffee'?
qs.why: Voudrais is the conditional of vouloir.

qs.q: The futur and conditional use the same stem for 'aller' (ir-).
qs.why: J'irai and j'irais share the stem ir-.

qs.q: Match each form to its meaning
Put the words in order: 'Tomorrow I will go to Paris'

lab.q: Challenge: complete in the futur: Je ___ (finir) demain.
Challenge: type 'we will have' in French (avoir).
Challenge: complete in the conditional: Je ___ (vouloir) un thé.

learn.b: Use the tu, nous and vous forms without the pronoun: Parle ! Parlons ! Parlez ! For -er verbs, drop the -s in tu: Mange ! Irregular: être gives sois, soyons, soyez; avoir gives aie, ayons, ayez; aller gives va.
For a negative command, put ne ... pas around the verb: Ne mange pas ! With a pronoun, it goes after in a positive command: Mange-le ! It goes before in a negative one: Ne le mange pas !

Take the ils form of the present, drop -ent and add -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent: que tu finisses. Use it after il faut que, je veux que and bien que. Irregular: que je sois, que j'aie, que j'aille, que je fasse.

qs.q: How do you say 'Speak!' (tu)?
qs.why: For -er verbs the tu imperative drops the -s.

qs.q: How do you say 'Don't eat it!' (tu, le gâteau)?
qs.why: In a negative command, the pronoun goes before the verb.

qs.q: Complete: Il faut que tu ___ tes devoirs. (finir)
qs.why: Il faut que is followed by the subjonctif.

qs.q: Complete: Il faut que je ___ à la banque. (aller)
qs.why: Aller has the irregular subjonctif aille.

qs.q: After 'je veux que', French uses the subjonctif.
qs.why: Wishes about other people trigger the subjonctif.

qs.q: Match each form to its meaning
